records.theme: Cross-border private transmission is becoming a prerequisite for Copperbelt mine growth
records.location: Kalumbila, Zambia to Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.why_surfaced: Named public, private and development-finance participants signed a framework for a 700 MW link after technical and environmental studies, explicitly tying regional power trade to mining expansion.

world_change: FIS-RDC, EnPower, Trafigura and Gridworks signed a strategic framework for a privately financed cross-border transmission line.
pressure: Copper and cobalt production around Kolwezi requires more reliable power than the DRC grid can consistently provide.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Bankable cross-border transmission, creditworthy offtake, tariffs, permits and coordinated Zambia-DRC grid operation.
formation: A privately developed 700 MW interconnector could turn Southern African surplus generation into new Copperbelt industrial capacity.
connected_companies_and_tickers: First Quantum Minerals (TSX:FM; indirect regional load/exposure)
consequences: Lower-cost and more reliable mine power
New export route for Zambian generators
Demand for substations, conductors and grid services
evidence: SADC project records and local French-language reporting

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 7 October scan; absent on 6 October.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: A signed multi-party framework, completed studies and quantified capacity establish a coherent mechanism, but financing and construction have not closed.
strengthening_evidence: The 6 October framework names the developer, trader and state investment participants.
Project materials quantify about 700 MW, 190-200 km and US$300 million construction cost.
weakening_evidence: The announcement is a framework rather than financial close or notice to proceed.
break_conditions: Cross-border permits or tariffs are not agreed
Mining offtakers do not sign bankable contracts
new_links: Copperbelt mine growth is explicitly linked to private regional transmission and SAPP power trade.

listed_players.name: First Quantum Minerals
listed_players.role: Large Kalumbila-area miner and indirect regional power-system participant; not a disclosed project sponsor

records.valuation_research: No project tariff, sponsor economics or attributable listed-company earnings are disclosed. Listed exposure is contextual and not a recommendation.

evidence.fact: The partners signed a framework to finance, build and operate a roughly 200 km, 700 MW Kalumbila-Kolwezi line with an estimated US$300 million construction cost.
French-language project reporting describes the same US$300 million private interconnector and its Copperbelt purpose.
evidence.english_summary: The report confirms a 700 MW, 200 km private Zambia-DRC line aimed at the Kolwezi mining region.

evidence.fact: EnPower says technical and environmental studies are complete and describes a 330 kV line with a 700 MW thermal limit.

contradictions: Published cost estimates vary from about US$250 million to US$300 million.
A framework agreement does not demonstrate committed debt, equity or offtake.
Regional generation availability may constrain actual imports even after the line is built.
